today.watching: Watching {{name}}. Looking for their job board…

how.title: Suggested from your matches, checked daily without AI

suggest.title: Suggestions (no AI).
suggest.body: A company is suggested when its jobs keep fitting you: at least 2 matches, or 1 you shortlisted, in the last 8 weeks. Every reason points to the posting it came from, or to the company facts already read for a CV. Nothing is invented. “Not interested” hides it for good.

find.title: Finding the job board (no AI).
find.body: When you press Watch, Applicamp looks for the company’s careers page on its own site and checks it for a Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby board or schema.org JobPosting data, the same readers the boards use. It respects robots.txt. If nothing is found, you can paste the careers page.

daily.title: Every day (mostly no AI).
daily.body: Each watched board is read once a day and compared with yesterday’s. Only new postings that pass your hard requirements (remote, countries, salary floor) go to the AI for scoring, in the same batch as the nightly search. Most days there’s nothing new, so it costs nothing.

match.title: A match (score 65 or more)
match.body: lands in Pipeline as Found and shows on Today: “Company posted a job that fits you”.

new.step: New postings that pass your requirements
new.price: Scored with the nightly search · about €0.0003 each

how.limits: Up to {{max}} watched companies. It counts against your limits (€0.30 a day, €5 a month), and nothing is retried past a limit.
